why does the swing desk hold 8 stocks and not 3?

It used to be 3. In the bot's own backtest from 2011 to 2026, momentum with 8 to 10 holdings traded about 3 times as often as with 3, made about the same, and had a smaller worst drop: roughly -42% to -47% instead of -57%. Spreading over more stocks also means each position is smaller (12.5% of the desk), so one bad stock hurts less. It's a backtest result, not a guarantee, but it's why the setting is 8.

can i paper trade at schwab?

No. Schwab has no paper trading, and every order through its API is real, so Kestrel uses Schwab for real money only. Paper trading happens in Alpaca's paper account, Webull's paper (test server) account, or simulated on your Mac: Setup → Settings → Paper trading happens at. Keep the paper amount equal to your real-money cap so the paper results are realistic.

how do i stop everything right now?

Use the emergency stop. In the app, press Emergency stop and type SELL EVERYTHING. From Telegram, send /kill SELL EVERYTHING (exactly that phrase). In Terminal, run `python run.py kill`. It cancels the bot's own orders, sells everything the bot owns with market orders, and halts both desks. It never sells your own stocks. If a sale doesn't go through, it keeps trying every 5 minutes, and you can also sell at the broker yourself.

what's opening_range_breakout

A day-desk method. The first 30 minutes after the open set the day's opening range, and it has no opinion while that range forms. After that, it buys if the price breaks above the range's high and exits if the price falls back below the middle of the range. Like every day trade, anything still open is sold 10 minutes before the close.

when does the swing desk actually make its trades?

Once a day, 15 minutes before the close: 3:45pm New York time on a normal day, 12:45pm on early-close days. That's when it scores its stocks and places buys and sells. The rest of the trading day the autopilot still checks the swing positions every 5 minutes, but only for stop-losses. It decides near the close because its backtest decides and fills at each day's close, and the same code runs in testing, paper and live, so what was tested is what trades.

which pushover alerts make noise

Kestrel uses Pushover's priorities. Emergency (2): a real-money kill switch or emergency stop repeats every minute, for up to an hour, until you open it. High (1): anything urgent, like a pause, a kill switch or a !!! warning, sounds even in quiet hours. Normal (0): every buy and sell, the after-market report, phase changes and warnings. Quiet (-1): everything else it forwards, such as daily results and lessons learned, arrives with no sound.

what is the new p&l calendar

It's the Profit & loss calendar on the Trades tab. Each weekday of the month shows the money made or lost on trades that finished that day, how many trades and how many won, and a Week column totals each week. A line above it sums the month: the total, up and down days, and the best and worst day. Blue is a gain and red a loss, and a deeper color means a bigger day for that month. Hover a day for details, click it for its trades, and use ‹ › for other months.

how does the swing desk decide what to buy

Right now (Stage 1) it uses momentum. At 3:45pm it lines up every stock it's considering, its watchlist plus up to 30 strong, affordable names from the daily scan, and ranks them by how much they rose over the past 12 months, leaving out the latest month. A stock in the top 20% that's also above its 200-day average is a buy, strongest first, while there are free slots (8 in total) and cash. If SPY itself is under its 200-day average, it holds what it has and buys nothing new.

how much does pushover cost

The Pushover app is free for 30 days, then a one-time $4.99 per platform (iPhone/iPad, Android or Desktop). Sending is free up to 10,000 messages a month. The Pushover tag in Setup → Your phone shows how many Kestrel has sent this month out of 10,000, and near that limit only urgent alerts go out. If you'd rather not use Pushover, Telegram also delivers alerts, and Telegram is the only way to send Kestrel commands from your phone.

why isn't it buying anything?

Several rules can stop new buys, and the after-market report lists the reason under its thinking. Common ones: all slots are full (8 swing, 3 day); SPY is below its 200-day average (momentum then buys nothing new); the desk is down more than 3% today; a strong stock has danger news or, on the swing desk, an earnings report within 3 trading days; the Risk agent is skipping a repeated mistake; the strategy has been paused by its own lessons; or it's the day desk's last 30 minutes. Sometimes nothing simply scores high enough.

what does beyond the price mean on a stock card

Three facts about the company besides its chart. Quality: its gross profits divided by its total assets, from the SEC, ranked against every US company (more profitable companies have earned higher returns). Insider buys: an officer or director buying the stock on the open market in recent Form 4 filings, not under a pre-planned schedule. Short interest: how much of the float is sold short and how many days of normal trading it would take to buy it back. Funds and banks often have no quality number.

how do i see the demo data

Choose View → Show Demo Data (made-up prices), or press ⌘D. It takes about a minute to build: made-up prices run through the bot's real code, including the study month, the plans and a few weeks of paper trading, so you can see every tab before the bot has traded. A DEMO banner stays at the top the whole time. Choose the same menu item again to switch back to your real data.

what's the difference between pause and emergency stop

Pause means no new trades, but nothing is sold: stop-losses keep protecting what it owns, and the day desk still sells before the close. Emergency stop is for when you want out: you type SELL EVERYTHING (in the app, or /kill SELL EVERYTHING on Telegram), it cancels the bot's orders, sells everything it bought (never your own stocks) and halts both desks until you resume. Pausing from the phone is /pause.

do the lessons last forever

No. Both kinds of lessons are built to change. Mistake lessons only count the last 60 days, so they fade unless the same mistake keeps happening (a relapse brings one back right away). Strategy lessons (half size, paused, conditions to avoid) are recalculated after every finished trade, so a wrong one goes away by itself. A fixed rule would stop the bot from ever learning that things changed.

how much of my money can kestrel actually use?

Only up to the real-money cap you set in Setup → Settings (the most real money it may use). The config default is $1,000, and your plan is $50 per broker, starting at Alpaca. The cap is split between the two desks (half each by default), and each desk keeps its own checkbook. On top of that, it never spends more than the cash the broker says is actually available, so it can't borrow or touch money meant for other things, whatever else is in the account.

how do i get a fred api key

It's free: sign up at fredaccount.stlouisfed.org, then API Keys → Request API Key. Paste the 32-character key into Setup → AI & news (FRED API key) and press Save; Kestrel checks it with FRED before saving it in ~/AITrader/.env. Then the Thinking tab shows the next CPI, jobs report and Fed decision with a countdown.

how do i hook up webull?

Apply for API access on the Webull website (API Management → My Application); Webull reviews it in about 1-2 business days. Once approved, generate a key and paste the App Key and App Secret into Setup, choosing Paper for test-environment keys or Real money. Press Test Webull, then approve Kestrel in the Webull app within 5 minutes (Menu → Messages → OpenAPI Notifications → Check Now → the text-message code). The approval lapses after 15 unused days, so the autopilot uses it each morning.

why is my strategy on half size

Because it's been losing so far. Once a strategy has at least 12 finished trades in that account and its average result is below zero, the bot halves its maximum position size: on the swing desk, 12.5% becomes 6.25% of the desk. It's re-checked after every trade, so once the average turns positive it goes back to normal. If it keeps losing clearly over 30+ trades, it gets paused instead.

is paper trading realistic or does it look better than real life?

Close, but not perfect. Alpaca's paper fills are simplified, with no market impact or slippage, so paper looks a bit better than reality; that's one reason real money starts small. The simulation on your Mac fills every order 0.05% worse than the quote to stay honest. Keep the paper amount equal to your real-money cap so paper behaves like your real account. And 30 paper days is a small sample: passing is evidence, not proof.

why compare tjr with random trades

Because a stop and a 2-to-1 target can look profitable on their own. The placebo buys at random moments in the same 9:35-11:30am window, with the same trend filter, stop and target, so if TJR's setup can't beat it per trade, the setup itself isn't adding anything. That was a real concern: in the 16-year daily test, TJR longs averaged +0.24R per trade, but random entries with the same stop and target got +0.18R.

what if the mac goes to sleep while the bot owns stocks

There are backups, though staying awake is the dependable setup. Every real position has a stop-loss order resting at the broker. When the Mac wakes, the day desk sells any leftovers the moment it can, since it never means to hold overnight. If the swing desk missed its daily decision, the Journal flags it. With lid-closed mode on, a weekday 8:30am New York time wake-up is also set, but wake-ups with the lid closed aren't guaranteed.

what is kestrel?

Kestrel is an AI stock-trading bot that runs on your own Mac, with a normal Mac app window (its own window, Dock icon and menus) to watch it. It trades through Alpaca now, with Charles Schwab and Webull as other broker choices. It works as two "desks": a swing desk that holds for days to weeks and a day desk that's in and out the same day, each with $500. The plan is careful: study the market, write a plan, prove it with paper (pretend) money, and only then trade real money, capped at $1,000. The "AI" is a machine-learning model on your Mac, not a paid service. It isn't financial advice.
